utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus, you are to continue with your examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. President and Your Honours. Before I do so, I just want to request if possible that the witness statements for Witness number 36 be given exhibit numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, let that be done.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, those witness statements, document ID number DD00-0362 and 0363 will be admitted as Exhibits P117 and P118 respectively.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Madam Witness, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I just have very few more questions for you today. First, I'd like to ask you, do you recall if the tram stopped when it was fired upon, or did it keep going after you were shot?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It kept going. Further down the street it turned around and stopped behind a building. It was a sheltered place, so those of us who had been wounded could get off the tram.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'd like to request the case manager now to show the 360-degree photograph of the location.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Madam Witness, we're going to see a photograph now, and I'm going ask you, please, to stop us when we reach the location from which the shots were fired.

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And now I'll ask the case manager, please, to continue to complete the circle. Thank you. Madam Witness, is this a true and accurate representation of the location where you were on the tram when you were shot?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'd like, please, to tender this particular 360-degree photograph into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P119, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court if you have any lasting medical consequences to your injury?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I have an 80 per cent handicap. My hand is not mobile enough. I can't drive a car. I can't write properly, and I have difficulty eating. Since I'm right-handed, I have trouble eating, feeding myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Marcus. Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Could we please have that image back, the last picture that was shown and tendered.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Witness, I would like to ask you something based on the statements that you provided to the Tribunal's investigators and a number of other documents as well. First of all, though, I would like to ask you to show me exactly what the distance was between the tram and the traffic light where the shadow falls, as it were. Where exactly was the tram? Was it rather close to the traffic light? Or perhaps you should tell us what the distance was.

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was roughly in the same area. I can't specify in terms of metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Right next to the traffic light then; right?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There's the shadow and there's the tracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you show me where the Metalka building lies since allegations have been made that the shots had been fired from over there?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's over there. Maybe I even saw a part of roof.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Where exactly?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There. Right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In relation to this building across the way from the traffic lights you mean?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus is on her feet.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I have three copies, hard copies, of this exact photograph. If it would assist the Court, perhaps we could enter one unmarked, and then I don't know if the witness is able or comfortable to mark, but it might be of assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, it may be of assistance. I'm to say that the e-court problems that we have experienced, that we experienced yesterday, I'm informed are resolvable and will be resolved, particularly after tomorrow when the -- there's a meeting between the court deputy and the parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I may, something about the meeting. We would be glad to have the meeting any time after trial. Today perhaps. However, it would be very difficult for us to manage 11.00 in the morning. You must understand that we are doing a lot of work to prepare for our cross-examinations. It would be very difficult to manage 11.00 in the morning. Right after our trial anytime.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. We've been advised that the court deputy will make a separate arrangement with your team, Mr. Tapuskovic. So you need not be worried.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I don't have anything on my screen right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: All right. The tram was near the traffic light. I'm not asking you to be dead accurate. Can you, please, show me how one can see the Metalka building from this position. The Metalka building is behind these buildings; right?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the Metalka is right there after this passage.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Quite far behind; right?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Metalka building is not that far behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I wanted to ask you when things were going in a circle here, you saw those two skyscrapers; right?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: The two skyscrapers are on the side where the BH army was?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: The two tallest ones?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You go behind -- across the river and the river was the borderline.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: The two tallest skyscrapers are in the Serbian territory?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note the speakers are constantly overlapping. It is impossible to interpret. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Did you hear that? The interpreters complain that you are both overlapping and that often happens when you speak the same language. So you must observe a pause between question and answer. That applies to both Mr. Tapuskovic and the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What I mean is the two really tall skyscrapers, the UNIS skyscrapers that were right near the tram, that was in territory controlled by the BH army; right?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Are those the two tallest skyscrapers in that particular area of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but they have nothing to do with the fact that I was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I won't be going into that now, but one thing I could ask you is this: Did you ever notice, looking at those two tallest skyscrapers that are as high as some hills, did you ever notice members of the BH army firing shots at their own citizens?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Were shots ever fired from those positions at positions held by the army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You answered a number of questions by the Prosecutor yesterday, and you said -- you had known immediately where you'd been shot from. That was my understanding of your answer. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I pressed my right hand against it, so that told me where the bullet had come from. It had to be from the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: We tried to reconstruct the setting, and you tried to show us which direction the bullet had come from. What about the police inspector who was in charge of the investigation? Why did they not try to reconstruct this event in the tram itself? You were on a tram when you were hit; right?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You were hit. You were injured. I don't doubt that for a second. You were on a tram.

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: A reconstruction was made, but this was done on the pavement and not inside a tram.

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Simply because no tram could stop there. The tram continued to drive further down the street. It took a turn, turned behind the building and stopped there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You weren't even in the same place where you were probably hit at the time, were you?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was on a tram and that's when I was hit.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will have to ask you some questions now about the statement that you made on the 15th of November, 1995. The document number, the 65 ter number, is 02875. This is page 1 that I'm looking at. Rather, page 2. The second page. I will do my best to ask you very specific questions. This was on the 23rd of November, 1994; right?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You say, "To my right was the Jewish cemetery and Grbavica." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. That was to my right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I believe you also said that you'd been hit from there. I think that's what you testified yesterday.

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I meant the neighbourhoods over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: But you did say yesterday that -- not right here, but yesterday you said you'd been hit from the Metalka building. How come?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I said yesterday is that I'd been hit from that direction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus is on her feet. No doubt a mischaracterisation?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Thank you, Mr. President and Your Honours. I do not believe that the witness identified the Metalka building. Perhaps learned counsel can point to the page and the line in the transcript from yesterday where the witness actually said that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What do you say she said?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: She said from the direction of the Jewish cemetery and Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I suggest you accept that -- accept that, Mr. Tapuskovic, that you have mischaracterised the evidence. Not intentionally, no doubt.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I accept that. What you suggest is entirely possible. I will have an opportunity to analyse this though and I'll be glad to accept my mistake for what it is. It is certainly not my intention to mislead anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Further down, paragraph four of your statement you say: "The confrontation line is quite near this area. I assume about 500 metres." That's paragraph 4. "I told her that she needn't worry," to your sister, I suppose, "because UNPROFOR, regarding that spot, they had an armoured vehicle there." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You go on to state, "I heard no shots. I just heard people screaming." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. People screaming and an impact against my shoulder.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Down towards the very last portion of your statement you say: "At the hospital they told me that six persons had been injured on that tram and that one person had been killed. The police told me that the bullet that had struck me was not a direct hit but, rather, a bullet that had ricochetted." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. The police told me nothing. When I was injured, we all ran down the tram. I tried to stand up and I asked my sister to come and help me because my arm was hanging loose. Then we got off the tram. There was a dead man there. I saw two other persons who were injured, and later I found out that six of us had been injured.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You gave this statement on the 15th of November, 1995, a mere year after this tragic incident that you were a victim of. How do you explain that in the light of what you're claiming now? Can you explain that to the Chamber?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave a statement at the time, but it wasn't the police who told me what to say. It was only what I had seen. It was only what I had experienced.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So you didn't say what we can read here?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not the way you've just read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not reading something that I'm making up as I go along. I'm reading your own statement. Is that your statement or not?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did give that statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I was going to ask you something about the other statement. Perhaps I'll just ask you this: In the other statement you make no reference at all, the 20th of November, 2006, that's 11 years later, you make no reference to what you originally stated a mere year after the incident. How do you explain that, what you said at the very end? Is this something that somebody told you to address?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have DD00-0376. I have no English translation of this document. However, it's a document that I was given by the OTP. This is an Official Note. If you could please have a look, and then perhaps you could answer two or three of my remaining questions, and that's about all I have. This is DD00-0376. Do you have that? As you can see, this is an Official Note, that incident on the 23rd of November. This was compiled on the 15th of December, 1994, by Kemal Buco. He's not a protected witness, is he? Kemal Buco is one of our next witnesses. I'll be asking him questions specifically about this, but I would like to read out a portion of this Official Note just to see whether this is something that was discussed with the present witness. Down the middle of the page -- can you see that Official Note in front of you, Witness?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking me, are you?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is there a translation of this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not that I could find.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm sorry. I'm told that the number for the English translation, the 65 ter number is 0059. If that will assist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I hope it does. Mr. Tapuskovic, you must come with the translation, and you know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I got this from the OTP, and I -- I thought all along that there had to be a translation. I looked high and low. My translations will only start to trickle in slowly. I have submitted a number of documents, a huge number of documents for translation. I'm not sure if those will ever see the light of day even until the end of this trial. Perhaps we will have a chance to review those later on. I was hoping all along that this would be translated. A witness will be coming soon who will be addressing this issue. I won't be dwelling on this. I have a single question to ask and the rest I'll be discussing with our next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ask your question, Mr. Tapuskovic. Let us move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a single question. I'll be tendering this document that was compiled on the 15th of December, 1994. Down the middle of the page the police inspector seems to have written this, "Given the fact that the tram was hit just there where the two of them where, her sister and she herself, and that the bullet had passed through an open window, there was no sound of glass being shattered. The passengers were hit by a single fragmentation bullet that splintered and Afeza was hit to the upper part of her right shoulder, the bullet exiting through her right upper arm."

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Is this something that you were shown when you spoke to the police?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, did the police show you what you had previously stated, that this had been a ricochet, not a direct hit?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about these military terms. I only know what happened to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'll be wrapping up my cross-examination because this is something that I'll be asking other witnesses about. There are several other statements, but I don't think there's any need to tire this witness with any further questions about the note that the police compiled based on this interview. This concludes my cross-examination. Madam Witness, thank you again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies. My apologies. DD00-0376, I would like to tender this document into evidence. And, if possible -- dated November 1995. Well, that's been admitted. That's 65 ter 02875 -- or, rather, I'm tendering -- rather, it's among the 65 ter documents, 02875, but I'm tendering this into evidence. This is the statement dated the 15th of November, 1995. I'm tendering this as possible evidence, those two documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The 65 ter number 02875 will be admitted as Exhibit D29. And the document ID DD00-0376 will be admitted as D30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, please. I'd like to go back to the question I asked yesterday. I believe that the Defence counsel went pretty much in the same direction as I did. Of course you're not a specialist. You're not a ballistic expert. You don't know much about shooting. But this is what I'd like to know: Yourself, did you have any concrete elements, concrete facts that could help us know where the shot came from? We must establish the facts, the fact that you were wounded, but we must also find who was liable, who is responsible for this. Experts will come, of course, to help us, but yourself, you know, you know what police told you at the hospital. You know what the physicians told you. But did you hear any shots? Did you hear any sound that could help us know where the shots came from, which direction and where it came from?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't hear the shot being fired. I just felt a very powerful impact, as I said in my statement, and I heard other passengers screaming and everything else that occurred just after. However, trams had been shot at before in that same place, and those were the comments predominantly being made by the people there. Those were the two buildings that were the closest to the museum, and those were under the control of the Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: No thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, that concludes your evidence. Thank you for giving it. You may now leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We have to take a 20-minute break to allow for some technical matters to be attended to in relation to the next witness, and the Chamber has some matters to deliberate on. So we'll take a half an hour break now. --- Break taken at 2.49 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The Chamber had to spend some additional time in deliberation, and the Chamber apologises, therefore, for the lateness of the resumption. The witness is here. The witness must make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You may sit. And you may commence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President, Your Honours. Might I just state just for advance notice, I'm going to be showing this witness various documentation, and it might necessitate the Chamber -- or it might necessitate my asking for leave to go into private session intermittently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. We note that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber has granted you -- Witness, I was just saying that the Trial Chamber has granted you protection in the form of face and voice distortion, so I will refer to you as Witness 138. Before we start, I'd like the court usher to hand you a document folded and I have copies for counsel and for Mr. President and Your Honours. Witness, do you see your name, your date of birth, your place of birth, and your father's name on that piece of paper in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you confirm to the Court that those details are correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: The details are correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President and Your Honours, I would like to offer that into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, it's admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P120 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I'm going to be asking some questions about the witness's personal background. I would ask if we could move into private session for that part of the examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, Witness 138, during your time as a crime technician, from the period you joined the force up until November 1995, did you investigate incidents of shelling and sniping?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Are you able to tell the Trial Chamber roughly how many incidents of shelling and sniping did you investigate in that period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: During that period I had 52 on-site investigations that concerned those incidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And are you able to say, within the 52 on-site investigations, roughly, how many pertained to shelling and how many pertained to sniping incidents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: I can't give you the exact breakdown. I took notes in my diary, but in terms of percentages, it would be about 75 to 80 per cent of the incidents were shellings and the rest were incidents involving rifle fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, I want you to concentrate on the period August 1994 through to November 1995 for this question. Again, how many incidents of shelling did you -- and sniping did you investigate in that particular period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: I think that altogether, when you count both sniping and shelling incidents, there may have been 20 or 25 of such incidents. I'm not sure. This is just off the top of my head.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And again the same question. Within those 25 or so incidents, how many related to shelling and how many related to sniping?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Well, the same statistics apply here. Many more incidents of shelling than of sniping.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now I'm going to concentrate on shelling. We will get to sniping at a later stage. Just take the Trial Chamber through a typical shelling investigation that you would undertake. Just describe the steps that you would have to take conducting an on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Before coming to the scene, an investigating team was established and I was part of it. Upon arrival on the scene, every member had his or her specific task. It was my task to examine the scene, to photograph it, to make a sketch of the scene. Of course, prior to photographing I had to mark every piece of evidence that I was able to locate, and then if it was in my job description to do so on that particular occasion, I was to take samples or to collect that evidence and to send it for further forensic analysis. When it came to shelling, it was not my task to collect evidence; in other words, fragments of the explosive, of the rounds. It was done by my colleague, and he would send those fragments on for further forensic analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: You said that a team would be established before, as you said, coming to the scene of investigation. Please tell the Trial Chamber who -- who was in that team and what roles did each person typically play?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Well, depending on the actual case, the composition of the teams varied. Sometimes there would be more people on the team, sometimes less. In essence, this was decided by the investigative judge who was in charge of the whole proceedings. The investigative judge would go to the scene, one or more inspectors from the security services centre that were working in the crimes against person section. Then there would be an inspector from the local police station, depending on the actual area. Member of the bomb squad from the security services centre would also be there. I was there, and possibly some experts that investigative judge requested to be present on -- at the scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, in addition to what you told the Court about examining the scene and photographing the scene, did you undertake any investigation as to direction of fire when it comes to shelling incidents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes. That was indeed one of my tasks, of course, in consultation with the entire team. I was one of the persons tasked with establishing the direction on the basis of the round that had exploded there; so the direction from which the round had come.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Did you establish direction of fire for mortar weapons and air bombs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Again depending on the actual evidence and traces on the site. Sometimes it was possible to do so, to determine this direction of fire on the basis of the traces on the scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: How would you determine the direction of fire from a mortar explosion? Just briefly take the Trial Chamber through that process.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: It was the easiest to determine that when mortar shells exploded on hard surfaces. In the Novi Grad area, this happened quite often because in most cases there was a concrete surface. A mortar shell leaves a specific -- specific impact site, impact print, and sometimes it was in the form of a ring and sometimes we referred to it as a paw. When a mortar shell impacts, there is an explosion and the actual shell itself fragments into a thousand pieces and the shrapnel leave their trace on the ground. It is now perhaps difficult to describe that. If you look at it, if you make a drawing, then it's easy to determine the direction of fire for that particular shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And what do you -- what about modified air bombs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Modified air bombs had a completely different shape and destructive power. Their body was not the same as that of a mortar shell. In other words, they did not fragment into many pieces of shrapnel. They simply made a very strong detonation, and they destroyed everything in a certain radius. On the basis of the marks left by the explosion, if such a bomb hit the side of a building and if there was a lot of ricochet, then you would be able to determine the direction from which this modified air bomb had been fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I just want to pick up on something you said about the destructive power. Can you describe the difference between the destructive power of a mortar and an air bomb, a modified air bomb?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: I lived in Sarajevo, and I could hear the sound that mortar shells made and the modified air bombs made. Unfortunately, I can tell you that the difference in the sound they make is immense. Second, when I would come to a scene and if it involved mortar shell impact, mortar shells caused less damage to the physical structures, quite unlike the modified air bombs which sometimes could destroy two or three apartments at once.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: When you speak about the sound, are you talking about the explosion sound or the sound in flight?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: No. I was talking about the sound of the explosion that I was able to hear on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Are you able to put into words -- or are you able to describe the difference in the sounds of both mortars and modified air bombs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Well, modified air bomb explosions were much louder than the mortar shell explosions. And the damage that the modified air bomb could cause, you could see from the damage just how powerful those blasts were. When I carried out on-site investigations in case -- in the case of air bomb explosions, on some occasions mortar shells would land 150 metres from where we were doing our job, but to me it sounded like firecrackers going off when you compare that sound with the sound of the modified air bomb exploding.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes. I will actually elaborate on your last -- on the last part of your answer in a moment, but I want to go back to the -- the destruction of physical structures that you spoke about. How about the destruction of -- let's say, the human destruction? How does it differ between a mortar and a modified air bomb?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Mortar shells are made in such a way that they have a body made of cast metal which is made in such a way that it fragments into thousands of pieces, and it's purpose is to kill personnel. The shrapnel have a large range, the shrapnel generated by the explosion. Only the other hand, the air bombs do not generated any fragments, but the fragments would be generated if it hit a hard surface, and then the pieces of concrete would in themselves become deadly fragments. But in our work we always encountered many more casualties if we were dealing with mortar shell impacts than with modified air bombs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: When you talk about fragments, is there another term that one could use to describe fragment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Shrapnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, I want to ask you about the difference between a modified air bomb and a mortar in terms of its accuracy. Are you able to talk about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Indeed I am. The mortar shell is fired from a mortar which can be adjusted accurately for the shell to land in an area that is normally about 10 square metres large. That is normally the targeted area. When you use a modified air bomb, the -- such targeting is not possible. When I say "modified," it means they weren't serially produced. They had special rocket launchers with special charges that they would attach to the tip of these modified air bombs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: We took a number of specialised courses. We worked on this. We worked with ballistic and forensic experts. We read literature on this and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: In your investigations of modified air bomb incidents, did you ever find rocket launchers on the site or parts of rocket launchers on the site of the investigation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, we've just been talking about your -- your role in determining the direction of fire of mortars and modified air bombs. Was it your role to determine the origin of fire of modified air bombs and mortars?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: That wasn't my job. There were other people who were in charge of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: What about determining the angle of descent of the projectile?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: We're talking about mortar shells, because they would have an angle of descent and then they would impact against a certain surface. I didn't measure the angle and I didn't establish what the angle was. There was a ballistics expert there who was in charge of those measurements, and that was his job, not mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, I want to move to some specific incidents. First of all, do you remember an incident at Geteova street number 12?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Geteova street.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Excuse me. That was my terrible pronunciation. Geteova street number 12.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember that explosion. 22nd of June, 1995. Geteova street number 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: On that day, did you conduct an on-site investigation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes, I did. There had been an explosion, and I came there with a team and I carried out an on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Who was on that team?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: There was an inspector from the security services centre. There was an inspector from the Novi Grad station. There was an inspector from the bomb squad. I was there, and I think there was a judge with us. I'm not certain, but I think that's what my report reflects.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Actually, that leads into my next question. Do you remember producing a report from your on-site investigation on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes. I produced one as soon as I was back at the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President and Your Honours, I would like to show Witness 138 Exhibit -- well, 65 ter number 02465, and I suspect it's of assistance to the court deputy, but the ERN is 00375077 to 00375078. And I understand that is pages 3 and 4 of the composite exhibit. And, Mr. President and Your Honours, I would like to, if possible, move into private session since there could be features that identify the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Okay. Witness 138, do you have a sketch on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Did you complete this sketch?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes. This sketch comprises this sketch itself and another, an A4 sketch. There is a brief explanation of this sketch and a brief description of events. On the front page you have my name, the date of the incident and the file number.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Right. What I would like you to -- at this stage, with the sketch in front of you -- first of all, can you explain the figures -- well, figure number 1, first of all? What does that denote?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Number 1 marks the place of the explosion. That is the exact place where the projectile went off.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President and Your Honours, I now find myself in a little bit of difficulty because I would like Witness 138 to mark this -- this sketch. I guess it can be done on the monitor now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, he can mark it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: You said that point number 1 marks the exact place where the projectile went off. Well, firstly, when you say "went off", do you mean exploded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: That's where it exploded.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you, beside the number 1 on the right, just put the letter E.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: [Marks]. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can I just inquire --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I can't see anything at all. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I apologise for being difficult, but is the letter E in the same colour as the figure number 1? I would prefer it if it could be done in a different colour. I'm grateful for the indulgence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, do you see the figure 2 there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: I see all the numbers quite clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: What does the figure 2 denote?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: The figure 2 marks the place where a part of the explosive device was found, and we used this number to mark that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Perhaps you can mark that with an F for "fragment." Is that an accurate reflection when you talk about part of explosive device?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes. We can say that, F for "fragment." F1 perhaps? Would you like that, because there are more fragments.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Well, do you see a position there where there was another fragment found and, if so, which number is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: This is number 3. Another fragment was found there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Very well. Can you mark that with the letter F and the figure 1.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, on that sketch, do you see the place where the damage was caused?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: No. Apart from the place of the explosion, you can't see that on the sketch, with the exception of number 4, which is blood marks. That's the place where we found blood marks.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Why did you find blood marks at number 4?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: In addition to other marks that I found, I also found blood marks. Someone was probably hit there and left bleeding, hence the blood marks. When we arrived to carry out an inspection, there were no injured or dead at the scene itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Did you find out later whether anybody had been injured or killed in this incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes. It's in my report. I found out from my colleagues who were part of the investigation team. They were in charge of finding out who had been injured and who had been killed. I later got the names from them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Do you remember who was killed on that incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: In this particular case, a two-year-old girl was killed, and her's is the only name I remember. Her name was Elmedina Burek.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Looking at this sketch, are you able to say where the girl was located when she was killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: The girl was in a cot inside a flat. The piece of shrapnel tore through the wall of this building and killed the little girl in her cot.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Is the wall of the building depicted on this sketch?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you mark it with the letter B, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: I'll mark the middle point, but it runs the entire length, and I mean both sheets. It's right underneath the mark where it says P16. That is the wall I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: That's fine. Thank you. Now, I just want to ask you about the figures that are on the sketch in the middle. Do you see those figures?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And what do they represent?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: These are elevation marks marking the distance between certain pieces of evidence that were inspected and marked, so that if the investigation was to go on the next day, these pieces of evidence could be returned exactly to the same spots where they were found or else, in order for us to be able to tell the distance between these traces, pieces of evidence, and the corner of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President and Your Honours, I'd like to offer that into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, it's admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P122, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I'm sorry, but I have a question. On this graph, the figure 2 that's at the bottom of the page means fragment number 1, but what is the figure 2 that is on top of the page? There's also figure number 4. Could you tell us what that is, the ones that are on the top of the page? There's a 2 and a 4 on the top of the page.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Certainly. Number 4 marks the blood, the blood that was found in that spot. The number 2 marks the distance between that and the corner of the building. You see this curving line right here and the corner. So this is the corner of that residential building. At a distance of two metres from there, you find the blood marks. And the 15.4 metres is the distance from there to the other opposite corner of the building. So that's what the number 4 marks both in the sketch and in the photographs that I actually took.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I'd like to now, sticking with the -- the same exhibit number, which is 2465, could we move to page 00375086. Before we do that, excuse me, can we move into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness 138, sticking with this incident, finally, I'd like to show you Exhibit 65 ter 2466. And the ERN is 00375110 to ERN 00375114, and I hope that these are photographs. Witness 138, do you see a photograph on your screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes, I can see this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Did you take this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes, upon arrival at the scene and once we've marked everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Just to -- just to confirm, this photograph relates to the incident that we're currently talking about, that is, on the 22nd of June, 1995 at Geteova number 12; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: That is correct. This is an impact site on the asphalt surface next to a building in number 12 Geteova Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President and Your Honours, just for the sake of completeness, I'd like to -- to interchangeably use the sketch that has been admitted with the photographs so Witness 138 can present -- help present the sequence to Your Honours if that's possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Let that be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness 138, do you see the sketch on the ELMO beside you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, looking at the photograph, do you see a figure number 2 there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Does that figure number 2 correspond to a marking on the sketch, and if it does, please indicate that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes, it does correspond. This is in fact marked accurately both in the photo file and on the sketch.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Well, just to be clear, there are, as I can see, two figure number 2s on the sketch. Can you point out the figure number 2 on the sketch that corresponds to the number 2 on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: The one that we're looking at on this photograph is the one that I'm pointing at right now. This might be a bit confusing because I put number 2 here and I didn't write this down here, but the point where -- that I'm pointing at where these two lines intersect, this is the location of this fragment that you can see here on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: For the --

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: For the benefit of the record, in answer to my question whether the figure number 2 on the photograph corresponds to a figure on the sketch, Witness 138 pointed at the figure number 2 that is on the bottom left-hand corner of the sketch closest to the figures 00375088. Can we now move -- keeping the sketch on the ELMO, can we now move to the second page of the photographs, and that is 00375111. Can we for the moment just concentrate on the top picture. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, do you have a picture on your screen with the figure number 1?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: What is depicted on that picture?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: On this photograph we can see the impact site, the explosion site, in other words, and the remnants of the projectile.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now again for the sake of completeness, does the photograph with the figure number 1 correspond to a mark or a figure on the sketch on the ELMO, and if it does, please, can you indicate that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. We have the same number both on the sketch and on the photograph. It is the same mark.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: For the record, the witness is -- the witness has pointed to the figure number 1 on the right-hand side at the bottom of the sketch. May we move back to the top picture, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness 138, while we're on this picture, since you've said this is the explosion point, were you able to determine the direction of fire from this explosion point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes, we were, because on the basis of the explosion and the fact that this tube got stuck in the concrete, we were able to determine the direction from which this projectile had come, and in fact I marked this on the drawing that I made.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Well, firstly, what was the direction that you concluded it came from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Well, you can see here that it came from the west.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Sorry, Counsel. Could you, please, ask the witness to show this again, because I didn't get it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour. I was just trying to get back to the ELMO. I noticed that the witness was marking on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. This arrow here marked with number 5 indicates that the shell had come from this direction and that it exploded at this point here that is marked with number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: For the record, the witness is pointing to the arrow on the bottom right-hand page of the sketch that is just above the markings 1, E. Perhaps, actually, to make it easier, could the witness put the letter W at the end of the arrow.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now move to the same page of the photograph but to the bottom photograph on the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Do you see a photograph on your screen, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: What is that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: This is a fragment that we found on the site. It is marked with number 2. It was photographed together with a scale ruler.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And actually, I forgot to ask you, but this photograph and the one before that and the words on top of this one, did you personally take these photographs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I took those photographs. I photographed the fragment that is marked both on the sketch and in the photo file with the number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, again, the same exercise. Looking at the sketch on the ELMO, does the figure number 2 here on this photograph correspond to a figure on the sketch, and if it does, please, indicate that for the Court.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes. This is the fragment that I'm pointing here on my drawing. I first approached it, then I placed a scale ruler next to it, then I photographed it from above.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: For the purposes of the record, the witness pointed to the -- the marking -- the area of the marking F, 2 on the bottom left-hand corner of the page. May we please move to the next page of the photographs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Excuse me, Counsel. Could you ask the witness what are the small signs that look almost like, I don't know, pigeon feet just south of the point on the map marked as 3, between the -- marked 3 and the wall. There are two groups of small marks, and what are they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yes. Exactly, Mr. Witness. What are they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is our mark indicating that this is grassy area. This is an area where there's grass, whereas all the rest is actually asphalt, and you can see that on the photographs. So this was a convention that we used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Did we arrive at 00375112, the next page of the photographs? I see that we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness 138, do you see a photograph on your screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do. I see a photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Did you take that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I took this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And what is depicted in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: This is where one of the larger fragments was found. It was marked with number 3. And you can see behind it the explosion site.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Just for the benefit of the Court, when you said you could see the explosion site behind it, can you point to it, and is it possible to mark this with an E?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: You can see in the photo file, behind number 3, you can see a dark area on the road. This is the explosion site, and this number 3 is the fragment that we marked with this number. And the explosion site in relation to the number 3, this is the direction from which I took this photograph. I wanted to get the location where fragment number 3 was from this direction, and then in the background you can actually see the explosion site. I don't quite understand. What is it that you want me to mark?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes. We will get to the same exercise with respect to the sketch in a moment, but I actually -- since you mentioned, you could see the explosion site on the photograph behind, as you said, the figure number 3. I would like you to mark that on the photograph, and I understand it can be done.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: So this is the explosion site, and this is the fragment that is marked with number 3. You told me to put a letter next to the explosion site?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I didn't, but I am now, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Which letter do you want me to put?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: The letter E.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I think that that particular photograph needs to be -- I'd like to tender that individually into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be admitted as Exhibit P123, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: All right. You mentioned in your initial answer to my question that -- that you could see the corresponding figure from this photograph on the sketch, and again I'd like you to go to the sketch on the ELMO and indicate that for the Court.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: The fragment that can be seen on this photograph marked with number 3 is here on the sketch where you can see these two lines with arrows intersecting, and it is marked with this number here, F1.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: For the record, the witness is pointing to the spot just beside the figure number 3, the letter F, and the figure number 1. Now, if we can scroll down to the second photograph on the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: So, Witness, do you see a photograph on your screen with a big, large figure number 3?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes, I can see this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And -- and what is depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: This is a photograph of the fragment that is marked with the same number on the previous photograph but close up and again with the scale ruler.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: So can I just confirm so as to save us going back to this sketch that this figure number 3 corresponds to the figure number 3 that you just indicated a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Do you want me to point to something on the sketch or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: No. I think it's fine. If you can confirm that this figure corresponds to the figure number 3 on the sketch.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. This is the fragment that we saw on the previous photograph, and on the sketch of the scene, it is marked with the number 3 or with the letter F1 which I put next to it a little while ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Okay. Can we now move to the next page of the photographs, and that is 00375113.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: So, firstly, Witness 138, did you -- do you see a photograph on your screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes, I can see a photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Did you take that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes, I took this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And what is in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: On this photograph we can see a section of the northern facade of the skyscraper or a high-rise building located at number 12 Geteova Street. And you can see on it, on the sandy area here, you can see the red stains. That's actually blood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may ask the Prosecutor, this is not marked with any number, this photograph. So far we've had numbers for each of the photographs, and that's been very useful. Do we have a number on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is there a number on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: No, Mr. President, at the moment there isn't, but I'm going to ask Witness 138 to provide some more explanations which should make everything clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, on that photograph that we see here, do you see an impact point on the wall in the photograph just above the sandy area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes. I can see the damage to the facade which occurred when a projectile or part of a projectile hit the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Did that damage to the facade that you speak about, was it caused by the projectile that exploded at the impact point that you have indicated with the figure 1 on the sketch?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: That's right. This damage was caused by a fragment of the projectile that tore through the wall and hit the little girl who was lying in her bed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: So behind the wall where you see the impact point, is there a residence at that -- at that place, an apartment there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. There's a residential building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Perhaps, Witness, you can mark the -- the area of the wall where you see damage with the letter D for "damage."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: This is the damage.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President and Your Honours, I'd like to offer that into evidence as an individual photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Let it be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P124, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, again, I'm sorry. This may appear laborious, but I submit it's ultimately helpful. Can you look at the sketch that you have and put a -- or indicate -- indicate on the sketch where the damage on the photograph occurred, if you can do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: You can't see that particular piece of damage on the sketch because this is the flank of the building, the flank of the wall, but it should be hereabouts. So what you see on the sketch is a bird's-eye view as it were, and this sketch was taken from one of those sides. Therefore, that damage can't be seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Very well. But taking that it is a bird's-eye sketch, you have -- where you have put the letter B -- do you see where you put the letter B there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes, I see the letter B. This damage would be to the right of where the letter B is. Which means in the photograph, too, you can see that it's closer to the left-hand corner of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Well, if you can, I'd like you to mark where you say it's closer to the left-hand corner of the building. I'd like you to mark on the sketch where that place is with the letter D.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: [Marks]. I've just done it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President and Your Honours, I'd like to tender that sketch as it now appears into evidence. I -- I have lost count, actually, as to how many times it's been admitted with different markings on there, but I'd be grateful for some --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, let that be done.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we've admitted this sketch with the first series of witness markings as Exhibit P122.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And it will remain Exhibit P122.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva, we are going to have to take a break now. We'll break for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, please continue, Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Counsel, can I just put a question to you to address to the witness. I'm just a little unsure about the date when this took place, because I think according to my recollection that the witness said that this happened on the 22nd of June. That's in my notes. But at a later point he -- the witness said that it took place on the 25th of June. So please check whether this took place on one or the other date. And secondly, we have seen on some of the photographs that were shown to us that there was a bloodstain that looked to me as if that had occurred outside the building, but I was confused because I thought that the person who dropped this blood had been inside the building. So if you can please ask the witness to clarify how the bloodstains got there. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: First of all, Witness 138, please just tell the Trial Chamber the date of this incident.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: The 22nd of June, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Does that clarify it for Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And secondly, Witness 138, if we could go to the photograph on -- again, I'm sorry to be reading out the ERN number, but it is 00375113. Do you have the photograph with the letter D on there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes, I see the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, when I first put this photograph up you were -- you explained that there could be seen some blood traces in the -- in the sand part of the yard. Do you remember that, firstly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that. It can be seen clearly in this photograph, although no numbers were used to mark it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: The question is, do you know where -- how that blood got to be at that location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: As far as I know, when the projectile exploded, a girl was killed, but several other persons were injured. Therefore, the blood probably comes from one of the persons who were injured.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: So from your answer, just to confirm, it is not the blood of the little girl that you have given evidence about that was killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: No. The girl came to grief inside the flat. This blood is not her blood.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness 138. Now, if we could move to the last two photographs, and that would be on the next -- actually, excuse me. If we can just go down to the lower photograph. I'm sorry. Okay. Witness 138, do you see a photograph there with the figure 4 on it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Did you take that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes, I took that photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And what's depicted in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: You can see blood from the previous photograph which was not marked with the number 4. It was first marked and then subsequently photographed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Is that the blood that you were referring to in the previous photograph just in front of the building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. It's the same blood as in the previous photograph under the letter D that I placed on the previous photograph. Here it is marked with the number 4, and you can see the exact spot. And the distance between this spot and both corners of the building was specified on the sketch.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And does that 4 on the photograph correspond to the figure 4 on the sketch?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Okay. If we can move to the last two photographs, please. Witness 138, do you see those two photographs on your screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: I see both photographs, one after the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court what are those photographs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: The first photograph you can see the entire body of the child who was killed. In the other photograph you see the head injury, which was photographed using a scale ruler.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And are those photographs of the child who you mentioned as Elmedina Burek?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes. And underneath the photographs you have explanations that I provided and typed up.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, did you take these photographs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: No. I wasn't the one who actually took them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Can we get away from this photograph now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. That can be removed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, you've just said that you weren't the one who actually took the photographs. Who took them then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: These photographs were taken in the morgue of the Kosevo Hospital by one of my colleagues who does the same job as I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Why didn't you take these photographs in the morgue of the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: When I arrived at the scene at the outset of the investigation, I had nothing to indicate who had been injured or who had been killed in this incident. Therefore, throughout my duties, which includes the moment when this incident, this shelling happened, I had been transferred to the Novi Grad police station from my original place of work. When we arrived at the scene, we found no dead bodies, and we found no injured persons. All we found were the pieces of evidence that I marked in the photograph. With the exception of these last two photographs that were taken by one of my colleagues, workmates, in the morgue of the Kosevo Hospital, they submitted the photographs to me so that I could attach them to the file that I was working on. At the time, this was standard procedure used to reduce the risk of physically going to the hospital and back.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: When you say that this was standard procedure, was this something that occurred on a regular basis, that is, you produced a photo documentation report with photographs, but photographs of casualties would be taken by other officers and included in your final photo documentation report?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Specifically, as regards this particular case, my bosses had agreed to do it this way. In all my other cases, I would photograph the scene, and I would photograph the bodies, the bodies that there were in the morgue wherever I happened to be. However, prior to our arrival, someone, and I don't know who it was, had taken this body to the Kosevo Hospital morgue. I wanted to avoid the risk inherent in -- by journey to the hospital and back, so my boss sent another forensic technician who then photographed the body of Elmedina Burek. He sent a messenger over to me with the photographs so that I might attach them to the relevant file.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: How -- well, put it this way: How was it established that this child was killed as a result of this incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: I didn't conduct the investigation on my own. The team comprised several people who were in charge of taking witness statements, the statements of those injured in the incident, and so on and so forth. So this is something that they learned, and they passed this information along to the investigating magistrate. The investigating magistrate or judge then gave an order for the forensic technician to go and photograph the body, do his job. They had probably found out that the body was inside that flat. I didn't take any photographs of the flat myself simply because back then I was not even aware of what had occurred. Later on we weren't even able to access the flat since the parents never came back.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: When you say that the team was comprised of several people who were in charge of taking witness statements, are you saying that the information about the deceased child was established by other officers speaking to witnesses at the scene?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: This was something that was done by inspectors of the security services centre and those belonging to the Novi Grad station. So yes, that's a fair summary.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I'd like to show Witness 138 a third document. It is part of the same -- the same 65 ter number, being 2465, and it starts -- it starts 00375075. And, Mr. President, Your Honours, might we move into private session since --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: -- it might -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Might I just very briefly seek some clarification? I have -- I intend now to show the witness further materials from that 35-page exhibit, that composite exhibit, for the purpose of offering it into evidence. If, however, it's been admitted into evidence, then I can move on. I just want to clarify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The answer is yes. Yes. However, Judge Mindua has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Counsel, before we move on to another question, I would like the witness to answer a question regarding the sketch, the sketch which he has drawn fairly well. Witness, on the sketch where we have figure number 1, that is the point of impact; is that right? And on the photograph on which we have the figure number 1 is a photograph of the impact, the point of impact. I don't have it on the screen, but I remember. So you conclude by saying that the shell came from the west. Your sketch shows that the south is at the bottom and the north at the top. The west is therefore on the left-hand side of your sketch. Is that right? Could you spell this out a little bit. I'd like to understand more clearly. On the basis of the facts you have provided here, you infer that the shell came from the west. In other words, from the right-hand side of your sketch. That's it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I've marked with an arrow was the direction of the incoming shell. The arrow in the lower part of the sketch, if that's the one you mean, that doesn't mark south. It actually marks north. We use the letter S to indicate north in our language. It's not the letter S as it is in English. The letter S stands for "sjever", which means north in our language. Does that explain it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's fine. That's fine. I understand much more clearly now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Before I move on, I'd like to offer into evidence the set of photographs that we've just been going over, and the exhibit number is a different one, being 2466.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be admitted as Exhibit P125, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, Witness 138, I want to talk to you about some other incidents. You've just been talking about an incident at Geteova number 12. Did you at any time undertake another investigation at that same street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes. I undertook other investigations on this same street but at a different house number.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Well, firstly, what was the house number, if you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: The building on Geteova Street, the house number is 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And when was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: On the 28th of June, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, in addition to this incident on the 28th of June at Geteova Street number 5, did you undertake another investigation on that same day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes. I was on duty that day, and I was at the Novi Grad police station. I had to perform several investigations following explosions on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: You said several investigations on that day. What was the first investigation that you undertook on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: On that day there was several explosions. The first investigation I conducted was near the radio television building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: What happened at the radio television building on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: There was an explosion in the -- in a courtyard of the TV building between studio C and the building across the way from the studio.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Do you know what type of projectile exploded in the courtyard of the TV building on at that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: It was one of those modified air bombs.
