utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Okay. I will show you some documentation regarding this incident, but just very briefly, can you tell the Trial Chamber how did you come to get involved in that investigation of the TV building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Word reached us that an explosion had occurred or, rather, I had actually heard the explosion myself. The duty officer in charge of passing information along to the security services centre informed us of what had occurred. A team was set up headed by an investigative judge and including an inspector from the security services centre. There were one or two of them. I can't quite remember, but you should be able to find that in the report. There was a member of the bomb squad from the security services centre and a number of other experts. I can't remember who specifically, but there must be a list of the people who were actually involved in the original report. I was a member of the team myself. I had to wait up for them to reach the Novi Grad police station from the downtown area first.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: When you say that you actually heard the explosion yourself, at the time you heard the explosion, did you know that the explosion was at the radio television building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: At first I didn't know because I was in a room and I couldn't hear from the walls. When you have an explosion like that, it's difficult to say exactly where it comes from, the direction. But the sound was clear, and after awhile we had received word from the policemen who were on the ground about this explosion and the duty officer who was in charge of the station at the time also subsequently told us that an explosion occurred at the TV building. Let me say something else. In addition to this explosion, there were another two roughly at the same time. This was sometime in the morning and I can't say right now with certitude whether this was the first, whether this one occurred before the other two that occurred on that same day. However, if you go back to the original reports, the exact times and the entire time line is stated accurately.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Very well. Just for organisation's sake, let's stick with the incident at the TV building. When did you eventually get to the TV building to conduct your on-site investigation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: I'm sure that an hour and a half or two hours had passed. It's specified in the report when the on-site investigation started. I had to wait for the investigating team to arrive from the town, and when we all met up there we went to the radio television building to conduct an investigation. It may have been an hour and a half, two hours after the actual explosion. I can't tell you with any certainty now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Sticking to what you did when you got to the incident side, briefly take us through the steps that you took in your investigation.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: We went into the radio television building. This happened behind the main building. It is a multi-storey building. The first thing we saw in this inner courtyard was that there was a great deal of damage. It was clear at first sight that this was not a mortar shell. After arriving there we approached the impact site of this projectile, and it was right next to the wall of the studio C. It caused a great deal of damage to the wall itself, and the wall is 60 centimetres thick or so, and it's made of reinforced concrete. This was the first case that I encountered of this kind of damage caused by an explosion of this strength. As for the walls facing this wall where the explosion actually took place, you could see other damage caused by concrete fragments from the wall and broken glass. And there was also a burn mark there. It's difficult for me to explain now, but you would be able to see that on the photograph. We determined at a later stage, because we could not -- we could not figure out how this explosion occurred, how this projectile hit the inner courtyard, but when we went up to the roof and when we were able to find some other marks there, indicative of how the projectile flew in, that made us conclude how the explosion actually occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: All right. I'm going to get to the -- to the diagrams and the photographs in a moment. I just want to ask one or two questions from your answer just to clarify. When you said that you were not used to this kind of -- this kind of damage caused by an explosion of this strength, what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Up until that time I mostly dealt with mortar shells or maybe shells fired from artillery. That kind of shell did not cause this kind of damage. The damage caused to this call was too great to have been caused by a mortar shell or a small-bore cannon. It was a 60-centimetre thick wall made of reinforced concrete.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Okay. At the conclusion of your investigation, that is the team's investigation, did you establish a sequence of how the explosion occurred at the TV building? First, tell the Trial Chamber if you were able to establish that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes. On the basis of the evidence we were able to locate during our investigation, we actually found enough evidence to determine where the projectile had come from, and of course it was quite obvious where it had impacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: At this point just -- just briefly tell the Trial Chamber the sequence of the -- the incident, and then we'll move to the visual aids.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: The projectile flew in from the same direction as the one in the previous case, the number 12 Geteova Street. In its trajectory, the projectile probably -- or, rather, definitely lost some energy, and it fell on the roof of the radio and television building. It ricochetted off it and continued along its trajectory. It flew over a low wall on the roof of studio C building, hit the building opposite this wall. It was actually taller than studio C building. It ricochetted off this wall and fell right next to the wall where it actually exploded.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: When you say that the projectile flew in from the direction as the one in the previous case, what direction is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: It flew in from a westerly direction approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Upon completion of your investigation, did you produce a report for this incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes. I produced a forensic report, and then I also produced a photo file and the sketch of the scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Might the witness be shown 65 ter number 185 and the ERN is 00358713 to 8714. And, Mr. President, may we move into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, Witness 138, do you see a sketch on your screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes, I do. The sketch, it is a sketch that I myself made.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, I want to try and take you through this sketch and explain a few things for the Court. On the upper left-hand side of the sketch there is a -- a circle with an arrow just behind it. Do you see that there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you just point to that with the -- with the stick, please, just to be clear.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: That's fine. You've marked it. That's okay. So what is that marking? What does that marking depict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: This is a mark indicating the damage to the roof caused by the impact and the ricochet of the projectile.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, in terms of the sequence, was that the -- well, where does that impact point come in the sequence of this -- in the sequence of the explosion in this incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: This is the damage to the roof of one section of the radio television building. I don't know what's underneath this roof, but the projectile flew in from the left-hand side, and you can see this arrow that's marked here. This is where it ricochetted off, and then it continued along this trajectory, which is a little bit hard to see on this photograph. And then it hit here, flew other studio C and hit right here at this wall, ricochetted off, fell down to the floor, and that's marked with AA on this drawing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness 138. Please don't mark the sketch unless I ask you to, because I want to get through this as clearly as possible. So that red -- that circle that you have made on the left-hand side of the -- on the left-hand side of the picture of the impact point, does that represent the first impact point of the projectile on the building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. As I've already said, the projectile flew in from the left-hand side. This is the first point of contact with the RTV building. It ricochetted off right back into the air and continued along a new trajectory.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Very well. Can you please mark -- can you please write on top of that circle the letters F, I for India, and P for Papa.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And just to be clear, is that first impact point on the roof of the building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes. That is the first impact on the building. It first hit the roof.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Did it explode at that point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: No, it did not explode here. It just ricochetted off and then continued on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Where did it ricochet off to? In other words, try and follow the -- follow the sequence of the projectile. Where did it go from this first impact point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: You can see it quite clearly on this sketch. There's this broken line with the arrows on it, and that's the trajectory that this projectile took. The broken line continues to the right from the first impact point, and you can see the arrows indicating the direction in which this projectile was moving.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you please with your red pen follow the line of the -- indicating the direction in which the projectile was moving up until the second point of impact.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, where the line has stopped on the -- on the wall, what happened there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: After it had ricochetted, the projectile continued its trajectory. It hit the wall here. It bounced off the wall and continued on to the wall of studio C.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Just to be clear, when you said, "It hit the wall here," please mark that position.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And is that the second impact point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: That's right. This is the second impact point.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you please put the letters SIP next to that circle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And just to be clear, did the projectile explode at that point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: No, it didn't. It ricochetted yet again.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Where did it go after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: The spot that I marked with the letters SIP, you can see an arrow there leading back to the left. It's a broken line. There's an arrow pointing at the wall of studio C, and that's where the projectile eventually came to a halt and exploded.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Very well. Please continue with the -- with your marker and mark the direction after the ricochet on the second -- from the second impact point to where the explosion occurred.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And just beside where the explosion occurred, can you please put the letter E.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, on the right-hand corner of the sketch there's a circle there, a large circle. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes, I see that. I drew it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Please explain what that is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Sure. Right here you can see the arrows, and it says AA. So that is a view from here to the place where the damage is apparent on the wall. Since this was drawn as a bird's-eye view, and you can't actually see the shape or the dimensions of the damage to the wall, I call this view AA, and I drew separate sketch of this. What you see in the upper-right corner of the sketch is a view of the damage to the wall of studio C and its dimensions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And when you say damage to the wall of studio C, do you mean where the explosion occurred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: That's right. The damage occurred as a result of the projectile exploding. This is the spot where the explosion occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And where the explosion occurred, what -- how would you describe that area where the explosion occurred, that -- that physical structure?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: It's a courtyard. It's an open area between the two buildings, and it didn't have a roof. This is where the projectile landed, and it eventually exploded next to the wall of studio C. There was a hole in the ground 2.4 metres deep. That was the hole in the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Okay. Now I'm going to show you some photographs, and we'll try and conduct the same exercise so as to get a clear picture of what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If the witness can be shown --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: One minute, Mr. Prosecutor. [Interpretation] Witness, please. I would like things to be clear. On the same picture, on the same sketch, we have studio C that's on the left. In the middle there's another room, and on the right another room again. So you're saying that the bomb exploded in studio C, but how did it enter there, because there's a wall. So did it go through the wall after having ricochetted elsewhere? It went -- it went through the studio's wall and then exploded in the wall, or how exactly did it happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My sketch clearly shows studio C. So that's a bird's-eye view. To the right there is the building of which the projectile had ricochetted. Part of the building is drawn. Between the two buildings there's an area with no roof. This building and studio C do have a roof. The projectile flew over the roof, ricochetted off the roof and handed in this area. This is not a separate building with a roof such as studio C or the building to the right of studio C. This is an empty lot, an empty area, a courtyard, if you like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand, but how did the bomb enter into the studio to explode in the studio? It went through the roof of studio C? Is that what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're right. I did not answer your other question. Once it had ricochetted off the wall of the other building across the way, it did not enter studio C. It hit the outer wall of studio C and that's where the explosion occur. The damage was outside, but also an opening was created on the wall of studio C. I put the letter A there, and I put it inside the studio, but I only did that in order to avoid obscuring any of the other features that are marked. The letter E should actually be outside studio C because the explosion occurred against the outer wall. Therefore, the explosion did not occur inside the studio, inside studio C; it occurred outside.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Before I move to the photographs, might that still be -- I'd like to offer that into evidence, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P127, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, for the purposes of this exercise, could I -- could I do what I did last time and keep a copy of the sketch on the ELMO so that we can see the sketch in conjunction with the photographs?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, might I just ask for 30 seconds to inquire of the 65 ter number of these photographs?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: It's Exhibit number 65 ter 194.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness 138, while that's being put on the screen, just tell the Trial Chamber, did you take photographs of the incident in your investigation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes. I took the photographs, I compiled a file, I sketched the scene, and I produced the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, do you see a photograph on your screen right now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Did you take that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And what is that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: This photograph shows the view that I found when I came to the courtyard, and it shows the scene of the explosion.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And that wall that you see on the left-hand side of the photograph, is that the wall that -- that is on the side of studio C that we saw on the sketch?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes. That's the left half of the photograph. There's the damage to the east wall of studio C.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If we can move to the next page of the photographs, please. May we please stay at the lower photograph for the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Do you see that photograph, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And did you take this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And what is that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: This photograph shows the damage caused by the first time the projectile ricochetted.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Does that photograph show the roof of the building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Indeed it does. The damage that occurred on the roof of the building. I drew a circle around it on the sketch a while ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And does that -- that mark on this photograph correspond to a mark on the sketch that you have on the ELMO, and if it does, please point to it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: The damage in the photograph is exactly what I'm pointing at on the sketch right now. This is how the photograph was taken. I was standing facing the damage. I'm showing you the spot on the sketch. That was my vantage point when I took the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: For the record, the witness has marked -- not marked, has indicated the small circle on the left-hand side -- upper left-hand side of the sketch that corresponds to the photograph that is being shown on the monitor right now. Okay. If we move back to the photographs and go to the upper one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: 138, did you take that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes, I did, while I was on the roof.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And do you see the entrance -- do you see the -- well, the entrance of the courtyard or the atrium in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Well, it's difficult to see it in this particular photograph. This is where it is. This photograph was meant to show the damage that occurred as a result of the explosion, damage to the other parts of the radio and TV building wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: On this still, are you able to mark with an arrow the -- the direction in which the projectile went into the atrium, if you can do this on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And where did it go down into the atrium? Can you mark that with an A.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: It's quite difficult. It flew over the wall and landed inside the courtyard. You can't see the inside of the courtyard from this particular vantage point, or, rather, the wall that the projectile later hit and ricochetted off. This is just the general direction. This was behind me. I was facing the other way when I took this photograph, the direction from which the shell came. But the purpose of this photograph was to show all of the other damage that occurred when the projectile exploded. If you go back to the previous photograph, it may be easier to actually see where the courtyard is located.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Very well. Let's go back to the lower photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can we -- sorry. Can I tender that into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, it's admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P128, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies. I might have missed something. What about the previous photographs? Those have not been tendered, have they, the photographs with the large-scale damage? Those have not been tendered yet, have they? Is this the first photograph that is tendered for admission?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is that so, Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: That's correct. Since this one has been marked, I'm tendering it as a separate exhibit, and I intend to offer into evidence the series of photographs once the witness has commented upon them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Okay, Witness 138, do you see that photograph on the seen where the impact point on the roof is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: Yes, I do. You can see the courtyard much better than in the previous photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, are you able to mark with your pen the direction in which the projectile took once it impacted on the roof?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: This is the path. Here it is where it flew over the edge of the wall and continued down to eventually land inside the courtyard.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you see on that photograph the roof of studio C, and if you can, can you mark it with a C?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Perhaps if you just put the letter P by the -- by the first arrow that you drew and then I will tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: That's P or "projectile." Your Honour, I offer that into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, it's accepted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P129, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can we move to the third page of the photographs, please. If it assists, I'm looking for page 00392144. Actually, it's the page before that. I apologise, Mr. President. That's not the one. I have hard copies available if it is more efficient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, it's coming up to 7.00. Can we get through it?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the President, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's coming up to 7.00 p.m. Can we get through this in a minute or two?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: The series of photographs, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The series. Then we'll adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Did I say that we'll resume tomorrow at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
